answer: Vesting with time-locks: every reward an agent earns is locked for 40 epochs and released in small slices, and only while the agent keeps passing live checks. The sybil operator pays: each fake must be run and fed real answers for months before a single coin unlocks, so upkeep cost grows per clone. Like an orchard that fruits only after years, a prism of copies splits effort, not payout. Survives a ring that dumps after a heist: unvested rewards stay frozen as onyx and are burned on the first failed check.
